briefing.opening: Good day. We now begin today's Climate Briefing for November 27, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Accelerating Warnings of Global Warming and Daily Life Struck by Climate Disasters
sections.content: The United Nations (UN) issued a grave assessment warning that global temperatures could rise by 2.8°C under current policies, as record-shattering temperature spikes in November trigger extreme weather events worldwide [9, 91]. Driven by global warming, the world's glaciers are projected to continue melting even if net-zero targets are met, while global damages—such as the expanding reach of infectious diseases and widespread ecological disruptions—are rapidly materializing [75, 83, 85]. In South Korea, agricultural and fisheries sectors have seen an entire year's harvest ruined by unpredictable heatwaves and torrential downpours, prompting the establishment of criteria to evaluate high-temperature crop damage; concurrently, marine heatwaves threaten the coastal disappearance of squid, one of the nation's staple seafood species [1, 11, 87].

sections.title: 🌍 Clashes and Outcomes at COP31 Antalya: A Turning Point in Climate Negotiations
sections.content: At the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), 46 formal climate decisions were officially adopted and Türkiye secured $26 billion in climate finance; however, the consensus process suffered major disruptions amid fierce pushback from the European Union (EU) against the leadership of China and Middle Eastern nations [14, 94, 95]. While the conference addressed the eight major achievements and agendas presented by UNEP—including methane reduction and sustainable cooling—clear limitations also emerged, including disputes over holding major polluters financially accountable and the unprecedented collapse of the proposed co-presidency model [12, 88, 92]. Notably, although the leadership of Small Island Developing States was highlighted during the negotiations, climate-vulnerable countries such as flood-ravaged Nepal continue to voice grievances over persistent gaps in tangible international solidarity following the summit [82, 93].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 RPS Sunsets After 15 Years: Domestic Renewable Energy Market Shifts to 'Long-Term Contracts'
sections.content: As South Korea's Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS) faces a phased sunset after 15 years, the market landscape is undergoing a complete overhaul toward a government-led long-term contract regime [47, 54, 55, 60]. Starting next year, the government will introduce competitive bidding for 20-year fixed-price long-term contracts—holding up to four bidding rounds annually for solar and two for wind—while shifting power generation companies from mere Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) buyers to direct investors [48, 53, 67, 72]. Consequently, the domestic renewable energy market is projected to transition into a framework anchored by large-scale, long-term investments, marked by the formal termination of the spot REC market in 2029, the rollout of KEPCO's long-term contracts, and the introduction of a new certification system, REGO [51, 56].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerated Carbon Neutrality Actions and Tech-Driven Adaptation by Local Governments and Industries
sections.content: At the local level, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province declared its vision to achieve 100% renewable energy by 2035 and signed a partnership with the Korea Environmental Industry & Technology Institute (KEITI) to revitalize the green economy, while Dangjin City committed 62 billion won toward the digital transformation and carbon neutrality of its industrial complexes [18, 30, 38]. Climate adaptation initiatives are also gathering momentum: the Korea Fishing & Farming Port Agency began in-depth discussions on shifting to smart aquaculture to cope with rising water temperatures, and the Korea Energy Economics Institute is advancing AI-driven cooperation to enhance renewable energy grid stability across Korea and ASEAN [3, 7, 52, 66]. In the industrial sector, on-site carbon mitigation is accelerating, highlighted by Korea East-West Power securing 672 MW in the centralized Energy Storage System (ESS) contract market and an automotive assembly plant deploying drones to expand on-site renewable energy installations [33, 42, 63].

briefing.closing: As the escalating waves of climate disasters threaten both industries and public livelihoods, structural innovation in energy systems and actionable adaptation measures are urgently required. This concludes today's Climate Briefing.
